system:
You are an art-world editor compiling a gallery guide. Answer with the JSON object the
schema describes and nothing else. Rank cities by the quantity, influence and activity of their
contemporary art galleries (commercial galleries, nonprofit and artist-run spaces), not by museums or
biennials. For every city give: the common English name; the country; a URL slug (lowercase, hyphens,
e.g. "mexico-city", "hong-kong"); the coordinates of the centre of its gallery activity; a map span in
degrees that frames the gallery districts (0.15 for a compact city, up to 0.6 for a sprawling one); the
IANA timezone; six to twelve gallery districts as short labels — combine adjacent districts with a
slash ("Chelsea/Tribeca") and never use a comma in a label — ordered from the busiest; two to four
metro_tokens: short strings that appear in a postal address inside the metro area (state or prefecture
abbreviation with surrounding punctuation like ", NY ", the city name, a postcode prefix); and one
sentence saying why the city ranks where it does.
user: What are the 25 cities with the most significant and influential art galleries worldwide, ranked by the quantity, influence and activity of their galleries?

cities.name: New York
cities.why: New York ranks first for its unmatched concentration of market-making dealers, blue-chip flagships and experimental spaces operating at a relentless pace.

cities.name: London
cities.why: London ranks second because its deep primary and secondary markets support a vast mix of international galleries and influential nonprofit spaces.

cities.name: Paris
cities.why: Paris ranks third after a major expansion of global dealerships reinforced its already exceptional density of historic and emerging galleries.

cities.name: Los Angeles
cities.why: Los Angeles ranks fourth for its large artist base, influential homegrown dealers and continuing influx of major international galleries across a sprawling geography.

cities.name: Berlin
cities.why: Berlin ranks fifth because its unusually broad ecosystem of commercial galleries and artist-run spaces remains globally influential despite a smaller collector market than the leaders.

cities.name: Hong Kong
cities.why: Hong Kong ranks sixth as Asia's strongest high-value gallery marketplace with dense international flagships and an active network of regional dealers.

cities.name: Seoul
cities.why: Seoul ranks seventh for its dense domestic gallery culture and rapid expansion by internationally prominent dealers serving a sophisticated collector base.

cities.name: Tokyo
cities.why: Tokyo ranks eighth because its immense but geographically fragmented scene combines globally respected dealers with numerous specialized and artist-led spaces.

cities.name: Mexico City
cities.why: Mexico City ranks ninth as Latin America's most internationally connected gallery hub with a particularly strong balance of established dealers and experimental spaces.

cities.name: Shanghai
cities.why: Shanghai ranks tenth as mainland China's leading commercial gallery center with major local programs and the country's strongest concentration of international outposts.

cities.name: Brussels
cities.why: Brussels ranks eleventh for its extraordinary dealer density, international collector traffic and experimental programming relative to its compact size.

cities.name: Beijing
cities.why: Beijing ranks twelfth because it retains a large concentration of China's most important galleries and artist-oriented spaces despite market and regulatory pressures.

cities.name: Milan
cities.why: Milan ranks thirteenth for its substantial roster of internationally influential Italian dealers and a growing field of younger spaces spread across the city.

cities.name: São Paulo
cities.why: São Paulo ranks fourteenth as South America's largest gallery ecosystem with powerful regional dealers and sustained international reach.

cities.name: Zurich
cities.why: Zurich ranks fifteenth because its compact scene has exceptional collector wealth and a disproportionate number of globally important galleries.

cities.name: Madrid
cities.why: Madrid ranks sixteenth for its broad Spanish gallery base and increasingly active clusters of ambitious young dealers alongside established programs.

cities.name: Vienna
cities.why: Vienna ranks seventeenth for a rigorous gallery culture that combines internationally established programs with an active generation of experimental spaces.

cities.name: Cologne
cities.why: Cologne ranks eighteenth because its historically pivotal dealer community remains influential and active even after some of Germany's market energy shifted to Berlin.

cities.name: Taipei
cities.why: Taipei ranks nineteenth for its substantial network of established East Asian galleries and an active collector market supporting newer programs.

cities.name: Amsterdam
cities.why: Amsterdam ranks twentieth for its durable concentration of respected contemporary dealers and nonprofit spaces despite a relatively small domestic market.

cities.name: Singapore
cities.why: Singapore ranks twenty-first as Southeast Asia's best-connected gallery marketplace although its dealer population remains smaller and more changeable than higher-ranked Asian hubs.

cities.name: Miami
cities.why: Miami ranks twenty-second for its growing year-round dealer community and strong collector access though gallery activity remains notably seasonal.

cities.name: Lisbon
cities.why: Lisbon ranks twenty-third for a fast-growing and internationally visible gallery scene strengthened by affordable space and an influx of artists and dealers.

cities.name: Dubai
cities.why: Dubai ranks twenty-fourth as the leading commercial gallery hub for the Gulf with strong regional programs and selective international expansion concentrated in a few districts.

cities.name: Mumbai
cities.why: Mumbai ranks twenty-fifth for its influential Indian galleries and rapidly strengthening contemporary market though the active dealer network remains comparatively compact.
